evidence.field: 大 entry; PDF p. 922, printed p. 907; continuation on PDF p. 923
evidence.text: The inspected scan shows the 大 headword and its form chart, labeled 商, 西周, 春秋, 战国, 秦, 《说文》小篆, 汉 and 楷书. It calls 大 pictographic and describes the oracle and bronze forms as a frontal standing person with two hands spread and legs apart. It proposes ‘adult’ as the original sense and connects that to ‘big’. The page 922 entry continues on page 923, where it says 大 extends to ‘big’ across dimensions and cites oracle-bone and bronze phrases using 大. These are the book authors’ analyses; the cited forms and semantic link were not independently verified here against their cited publications or dated artifacts.

evidence.text: The inspected record identifies an oracle-bone example as 合集21022 and a bronze example as 集成01472; it describes 大 as a frontal standing human with head, torso and limbs. This supports the broad human-figure account, but does not settle the book’s more specific claim that the arms are spread outward or establish the graph’s original sense.

evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析 / 大 / 形義通解
evidence.text: The account describes 大 as a frontal standing person with arms hanging down, proposes ‘adult’ (contrasted with child) as an original sense, and derives ‘big’ from that contrast. It cites the bronze phrase 郘鐘「大鐘八聿(肆)」 for ‘big’ opposite 小, and says early 大 and 夫 were one graph before 夫 acquired a short added stroke. The arms-down description differs from 字源’s arms-spread description; both interpret the graph as a human figure. The cited inscription and proposed semantic development are the source’s claims, not a dated sequence independently established in this research.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 漢字甲骨部件分析：大

evidence.field: 大 entry and Duan Yucai commentary
evidence.text: The entry gives the Eastern Han dictionary explanation that 大 depicts a human figure, and records 大 as an ancient form of 亣. Duan Yucai comments that 大 and 亣 are one character with slightly different forms, later placed in separate sections. This documents a historical explanation and commentary, not independent proof of prehistoric origin.
evidence.title: 說文解字「大」

evidence.source: 金真姬,《常用漢字二百字探源》
evidence.text: The inspected PDF lists oracle-bone occurrences 合集33788 and 合集6692, later forms including bronze and Warring States examples, and quotes the Shuowen account. It says the shape changed little from oracle-bone script to regular script, describes 大 as a frontal human form in contrast with 人 shown in profile, and gives examples of 大 used for ‘big’ in oracle-bone and bronze texts. This is an independent scholarly account, but its claim that the graph’s original sense was ‘person’ and later extended to ‘big’ is an analysis, not a dated semantic chain demonstrated in the cited examples.
evidence.title: 常用漢字二百字探源
